{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are given a JSON input with two parts: 'system_profile' describing installed software (product names and versions) and 'advisories', a supplied list of CVE advisories, each with its ID, description, and affected-version information. Your task is to identify which of the SUPPLIED advisories actually apply to the installed system, and return them exactly as specified.

Follow this procedure carefully:

1. PARSE THE INVENTORY. Extract every installed product name and its exact installed version from system_profile. Note version numbers precisely, including all segments (e.g., 1.2.3.4 has four segments; 1.2 is not the same as 1.2.0).

2. MATCH PRODUCTS, NOT KEYWORDS. For each advisory, determine whether it concerns a product that is actually installed. Advisory identifiers, descriptions, and affected fields may render product names differently than the inventory does: names may be title-cased (e.g., 'Openssl'), lowercased, vendor-prefixed or vendor-stripped (e.g., 'Apache Log4j' vs 'Log4j'), or use package-manager style aliases (e.g., 'openssl' for 'OpenSSL'). Normalize names (case-insensitive, strip vendor prefixes, common package-manager aliases, and punctuation) before deciding there is no match. Do not match merely because a product name appears in the advisory description text; the advisory must actually be about that product.

3. EVALUATE VERSION BOUNDS. Affected information may be given as structured fields (e.g., affected_versions, version ranges, less_than/greater_than style conditions) or described in prose within the description. Carefully determine the affected version range and compare it against the installed version:
   - If the advisory states a version range (e.g., 'versions before X', 'versions up to and including X', 'versions from A to B', 'affected versions >= X'), the installed version applies ONLY if it falls inside the stated bounds. Pay close attention to whether the bound is inclusive ('up to and including', 'through', '<=') or exclusive ('before', 'less than', '<').
   - If the installed version sits exactly on an inclusive bound, it IS applicable. If it sits on an exclusive bound, it is NOT applicable.
   - If the installed version is above the stated maximum affected version, it is NOT applicable (the vulnerability was fixed). If the installed version is below the stated minimum affected version, it is NOT applicable.
   - When the bound is stated in prose (e.g., 'users should upgrade to 2.5.1; all versions prior are affected'), translate that into the same inclusive/exclusive logic before comparing.
   - Compare versions numerically segment by segment; do not compare them as strings (2.10 is greater than 2.9).

4. DECIDE APPLICABILITY. An advisory is applicable if and only if (a) the affected product is installed, and (b) the installed version falls within the advisory's affected version range. If either condition fails, the advisory must be excluded — even if the product is installed, if the installed version is outside the affected range, do not include it. Conversely, if both conditions hold, include it even if the advisory seems minor, the product name is rendered unusually, or the version bounds are phrased in prose.

5. USE ONLY SUPPLIED IDS. Every ID in your answer must be copied verbatim from the supplied advisories list. Never invent CVE IDs, never include IDs from your general knowledge, and never include an advisory ID you were not given, even if you know a real-world CVE applies.

6. NO DUPLICATES. Each applicable ID must appear at most once in the output array.

7. OUTPUT FORMAT. Return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with no additional text, explanation, markdown, or code fences. If no supplied advisories apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.

Before finalizing, re-check each included ID against the version bounds (especially inclusive vs exclusive boundaries) and re-check each excluded ID to confirm the product truly is not installed or the version truly is outside the range. Err toward including advisories whose bounds genuinely cover the installed version, and toward excluding those whose bounds do
